title: Hom-tower representative and scalar-adjunction comparison
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R$, uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$, $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For every scheme $W$ use a small skeleton of $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$, completed coefficient sheaf $R_W=\lim_n(A_n)_W$, and ordinary unbounded module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. On the vertical sequence site write $\mathcal Q_W(n,U)=(A_n)_W(U)$, $R_W^{\mathrm{const}}$ for the constant sequence ring, $\mathscr P$ for the one-point sequence topos, and $\mathcal A=(A_n)_n$ for its quotient ring [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site]. Let $\rho_W:(W^{\mathrm{Tow}},\mathcal Q_W)\to(W^{\mathrm{Tow}},R_W^{\mathrm{const}})$ and $\rho_0:(\mathscr P,\mathcal A)\to(\mathscr P,R)$ be scalar restriction morphisms. Write $g_W^{\mathcal Q}$ and $g_W^R$ for point-sections morphisms to these one-point sequence topoi, with $g_W^R\rho_W=\rho_0g_W^{\mathcal Q}$. The symbol $Rg_*$ means derived sections with values in towers, without inverse limit. Restriction $\rho_*$ is exact. Use the derived internal Hom and signed closed tensor-Hom structure [def-pur-derived-internal-hom, def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model].
Let $K\in D(R_W)$ and $N\in D(\mathcal Q_W)$. Put $V=\operatorname{const}K$, $M=L\rho_W^*V$, $D_N=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal Q_W}(M,N)$, and $h_N=Rg_{W*}^{\mathcal Q}D_N$. Choose a flat-term K-flat representative $P\to K$ and a K-injective representative $I$ of $\rho_{W*}N$ in the category of constant-$R_W$ towers (equivalently, over $R_W^{\mathrm{const}}$ on the sequence site) [def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-pc-kflat-resolution, def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Let $\mathsf H_N(K)$ be the localization of the strict tower of global Hom complexes $\operatorname{Hom}_{R_W}^{\bullet}(P,I_n)$, whose transitions are postcomposition by those of $I$ [def-pur-hom-complex].
There are canonical isomorphisms of derived towers, natural contravariantly in $K$ and covariantly in $N$,
$$\mathsf H_N(K)\cong Rg_{W*}^R R\mathcal Hom_{R_W^{\mathrm{const}}}(V,\rho_{W*}N)\cong\rho_{0*}h_N.$$
The internal comparison $\rho_{W*}D_N\cong R\mathcal Hom_{R_W^{\mathrm{const}}}(V,\rho_{W*}N)$ is the scalar internal-Hom isomorphism of [lem-sfb-dc-hom-scalar-adjunction] for the ring map $R_W^{\mathrm{const}}\to\mathcal Q_W$ on the sequence site, where $M=L\rho_W^*V$ is the derived scalar extension; it carries evaluation, after the scalar-extension unit, to restricted quotient-linear evaluation. Its representing bijections for every $T\in D(R_W^{\mathrm{const}})$ are
$$\operatorname{Hom}(T,\rho_{W*}D_N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(L\rho_W^*T\otimes^L M,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(L\rho_W^*(T\otimes^LV),N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(T\otimes^LV,\rho_{W*}N).$$
The first isomorphism has the actual representative $g_{W*}^R\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\operatorname{const}P,I)$; its $n$th component is the stated global Hom complex. At every $n$ the comparisons identify
$$\operatorname{ev}_n\mathsf H_N(K)\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_{R_W}(K,\operatorname{Res}_nN_n)\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_{W,A_n}(K_n,N_n),$$
where $K_n=K\otimes^L_{R_W}(A_n)_W$ is derived scalar extension along the completion projection [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], $N_n=\operatorname{ev}_nN$ and global derived Hom means derived sections of internal Hom. The second finite isomorphism is the extension-restriction adjunction normalized by the actual reduction unit; these are isomorphisms of complexes in $D(R)$, not merely bijections of degree-zero Hom sets. No flatness of $R_W\to(A_n)_W$ is assumed.

source.note: Agent-formulated subargument, not a theorem asserted verbatim in the blueprint or Stacks. Foundational Stacks tags: 06YS, 0A95, 08J9, 07A6. The complete retained argument and exact Stacks labels are in report.md.

proof.text: Use the exact constant-ring sequence-module equivalence to regard $\rho_{W*}N$ as an object of $D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(R_W)))$. The site and the index category are small, so this tower category is Grothendieck abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-small-module-diagrams-grothendieck]; it has K-injective resolutions by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-functorial-existence]. Choose $I$ in that category, not by independently resolving its components. By [lem-weil-tower-evaluation-kinjective], every $I_n$ is K-injective and represents $\operatorname{Res}_nN_n$. Choose the flat-term K-flat $P\to K$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The exact equivalence [lem-pur-constant-sequence-module-equivalence] preserves acyclic complexes and homotopies, hence identifies this $I$ with a K-injective sequence-site complex.

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, exact left adjoint to constant-ring evaluation); injectives.tex Tag 079P. Constant-ring sequence-site realization.

proof.text: The constant complex $\operatorname{const}P$ is K-flat over $R_W^{\mathrm{const}}$. Indeed, under [lem-pur-constant-sequence-module-equivalence], tensoring a tower $C$ with $\operatorname{const}P$ has component $\operatorname{Tot}(C_n\otimes_{R_W}P)$: the sheaf tensor is the sheafification of the componentwise presheaf tensor, vertical covers give componentwise sheafification, and the signed sums in [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] are componentwise. An acyclic tower has every $C_n$ acyclic by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. Each displayed total is acyclic by [def-pc-kflat-complex], so the tower total is acyclic. The same componentwise exactness test shows that the terms of $\operatorname{const}P$ are flat, since the terms of $P$ are flat. This is a direct application of the definition of K-flatness, not flatness of any quotient ring map.

source.place: Tag 0940 (section-derived-limits), vertical sequence topology; Tag 06YN (definition-K-flat), tested componentwise on constant-ring towers.

proof.text: Put $J=\mathcal Hom^\bullet_{R_W^{\mathrm{const}}}(\operatorname{const}P,I)$. Its component at $n$ is literally $\mathcal Hom^\bullet_{R_W}(P,I_n)$. To check this, localize the sequence site at $(n,U)$. Its objects have indices $k\le n$. A map from a constant source $F$ to the target on this slice is determined by its map $F|_U\to I_n|_U$; its component at $k$ must be the composite with $I_n\to I_k$. These formulas give inverse maps and respect vertical restriction. Apply the slice definition [def-pur-sheaf-hom] to each pair of degrees and the product formula [def-pur-hom-complex]. The differential on both sides is $d_I f-(-1)^r f d_P$ in degree $r$; restriction from $n+1$ to $n$ is postcomposition by $I_{n+1}\to I_n$. By [lem-pur-hom-complex-global-cochains], applying $g_{W*}^R$ gives exactly the strict tower $\operatorname{Hom}_{R_W}^\bullet(P,I_n)$, with its actual differential and transitions. All identifications are $R$-linear.

source.place: Tag 0A8X (section-hom-complexes), global complex equation 0A8Z; sites-modules.tex Tag 04TT (section-internal-hom); vertical sequence slice ending at n.

proof.text: By [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], $J$ represents $R\mathcal Hom_{R_W^{\mathrm{const}}}(V,\rho_{W*}N)$. Step 2 and [lem-coef-hom-kflat-into-kinjective-independent-coefficients] show that this actual Hom complex is K-injective on the sequence site. Thus its direct image $g_{W*}^R J$ computes the total right derived direct image, without another resolution. Step 3 identifies its localization with $\mathsf H_N(K)$ and proves the first asserted isomorphism in the ordinary derived category of $R$-module towers. In particular the representative assertion concerns the whole strict system.

source.place: Tags 0A95 (lemma-RHom-well-defined), 0A96 (lemma-RHom-from-K-flat-into-K-injective), and Section 08J7 (section-internal-hom); total direct image on K-injectives.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-dc-hom-scalar-adjunction] on the same small sequence site, with ring map $R_W^{\mathrm{const}}\to\mathcal Q_W$, input $V$, and target $N$. Its derived scalar extension is precisely $M$, so its conclusion is $\rho_{W*}D_N\cong R\mathcal Hom_{R_W^{\mathrm{const}}}(V,\rho_{W*}N)$. The representing bijections in that statement are, in order, scalar adjunction followed by closed transposition, the strong tensor comparison $L\rho_W^*T\otimes^L L\rho_W^*V\cong L\rho_W^*(T\otimes^LV)$, and scalar adjunction again. They are exactly the three displayed bijections of the item for every $T$. The normalization clause of the cited statement says that the transpose is restricted quotient-linear evaluation after the scalar-extension unit. Thus this is the required internal comparison, including its specified evaluation, with no flatness hypothesis.

source.place: Tags 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), 08J9 (lemma-internal-hom); the evaluation-normalized generic scalar internal-Hom isomorphism, applied on the sequence site.

proof.text:
Apply $Rg_{W*}^R$ to the inverse of the isomorphism in step 5. For the two factorizations of $g_W^R\rho_W=\rho_0g_W^{\mathcal Q}$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. Since $\rho_{W*}$ and $\rho_{0*}$ are exact, their total derived functors are these restrictions themselves. The resulting comparison is
$$Rg_{W*}^R R\mathcal Hom(V,\rho_{W*}N)\cong Rg_{W*}^R\rho_{W*}D_N\cong R(g_W^R\rho_W)_*D_N\cong\rho_{0*}Rg_{W*}^{\mathcal Q}D_N=\rho_{0*}h_N.$$
These composition isomorphisms live on the one-point sequence topos; no inverse limit has been applied. Together with step 4 this gives both asserted isomorphisms of derived towers.

source.place: Tag 0D6E (lemma-derived-pushforward-composition); exact scalar restriction from Tag 07A6 (lemma-adjoint) specialized to an identity-topos ring map.

proof.text: Exact evaluation of the strict representative in step 3 has localization $Q\operatorname{Hom}_{R_W}^\bullet(P,I_n)$. Step 1 gives a K-injective $I_n$ representing $\operatorname{Res}_nN_n$. Hence [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] and [lem-coef-hom-kflat-into-kinjective-independent-coefficients], now on $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$, show that this complex computes $R\Gamma\,R\mathcal Hom_{R_W}(K,\operatorname{Res}_nN_n)$. This proves the first finite isomorphism as an object of $D(R)$. Evaluation and localization agree because evaluation is exact, by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. The same constant-ring tower resolution gives all these identifications; its transition at $m\ge n$ is literally postcomposition by $I_m\to I_n$.

source.place: Tags 0A96 and 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, constant-ring evaluation argument); the actual representative computes the finite derived sections.

proof.text:
For the ring map $R_W\to(A_n)_W$, [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] identifies derived scalar extension of $K$ with the stated $K_n$, represented by $P\otimes_{R_W}(A_n)_W$. Apply [lem-sfb-dc-hom-scalar-adjunction] to $K,N_n$ and this map, then apply derived sections. The coefficient-restriction/sections composition isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] gives
$$R\operatorname{Hom}_{R_W}(K,\operatorname{Res}_nN_n)\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_{W,A_n}(K_n,N_n)$$
in $D(R)$, retaining the scalar action through $R\to R_W$. This is a comparison of whole derived section complexes. Its transpose sends a homogeneous map $f$ to the map $p\otimes a\mapsto a f(p)$, and its unit sends $p\mapsto p\otimes1$, as specified in [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. It is therefore normalized by the actual reduction unit, with the signs of the fixed Hom complex and tensor-Hom structure. This construction requires no flatness of $R_W\to(A_n)_W$.

Finally these constructions are independent of the representatives and natural contravariantly in $K$ and covariantly in $N$. Indeed, [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined] makes the internal-Hom model in step 4 descend in both variables; derived direct image is already a functor. Its identification with the strict global Hom tower is the literal slice-and-sections formula of step 3, which commutes with precomposition in $P$ and postcomposition in $I$. The scalar isomorphism of step 5 and composition comparisons of step 6 are natural by their cited statements. Transporting along step 4 therefore supplies the canonical functorial structure on $\mathsf H_N(K)$ and both natural isomorphisms. Inverting quasi-isomorphisms preserves these equations, so this proves naturality for derived morphisms, not only chosen chain maps.

tool_uses.why: Identifies constant-ring sequence modules with literal towers, retaining sections and transitions; a generic realization tool.
Provides the Grothendieck hypothesis for the small constant-ring tower category, needed for a simultaneous resolution.
Supplies a simultaneous K-injective tower resolution from the Grothendieck hypothesis.
Supplies a flat-term K-flat representative on the small ringed site.
Provides componentwise exactness for testing acyclicity and evaluation/localization.
Identifies global sections of internal Hom with the external signed Hom complex.
Provides the generic evaluation-normalized scalar internal-Hom isomorphism on the sequence site and each fiber.
Provides the canonical comparison for both ringed-topos factorizations and for finite sections; no same-unit node states this generic composition result.
Provides exact scalar restriction and the actual p to p tensor 1 unit and tensor-transpose formulas.
Computes finite derived scalar extension on the chosen K-flat representative.
Provides representative invariance so the whole-system construction descends in both variables.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q147-e1cfce463 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read all of it: the item, all 9 steps and the 20 cited statements. The base node is the unsplit statement-only node that Q131 created; the 2026-10-21 re-split note applies to its resolved parent, not to this item. There are 2 accepted statement repairs. First, the base used K_n without defining it; the delivery defines K_n=K⊗^L_{R_W}(A_n)_W via lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings, matching how the parent and both siblings define it. Second, 'simultaneous K-injective' now says I is resolved in constant-R_W towers. Nothing else is weakened. The steps check against their cited statements. S1: Tow(Mod R_W)=Fun(N^op,Mod) is Grothendieck (small-module-diagrams), resolved by kinjective-functorial-existence, I_n K-injective by tower-evaluation-kinjective, and the equivalence preserves K-injectivity. S2: sheafification on the sequence site is componentwise because the vertical slice generates a cofinal covering sieve, so const P is K-flat with flat terms. S3: I checked the slice formula; (n,U) is final in its slice, so a map from a constant sheaf is fixed by its level-n component, and global-cochains gives the global Hom tower. S4: lem-coef-hom-kflat-into-kinjective (same unit, unbounded) makes J K-injective. S5: lem-sfb-dc-hom-scalar-adjunction applied to R^const→Q_W gives the bijections and the evaluation normalization (old step 3 used projection-mate-exact). S6: the composition lemma for both factorizations, with exact restriction. S7: evaluation of the K-injective Hom computes RΓ RHom. S8: the finite adjunction with p↦p⊗1 and p⊗a↦a f(p) from sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction (1),(2), no flatness. S9: naturality via rhom-well-defined. Q131's old steps 1-3 are all retained, and the 3 citers' uses stay valid. Small cases: K=R_W/ϖ keeps Tor; K=R_W; K or N zero; N concentrated at one level.
